subject: chemistry

points.text: An ion or molecule that donates a pair of electrons to the central metal atom or ion.

subject: chemistry

points.text: The number of donor atoms bonded directly to the central metal.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:crystal field splitting
text: Define crystal field splitting.

points.text: The separation of the d orbitals into groups of different energy, caused by the approach of the ligands.

subject: chemistry

points.text: The list of ligands in the order of their increasing ability to split the d orbitals.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a coordination compound
text: Define a coordination compound.

points.text: A compound in which a central metal atom or ion is bonded to a set of ions or molecules by coordinate bonds.

subject: chemistry

text: Define a complex ion.

points.text: An ion with a central metal bonded to surrounding ligands, such as [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:the central metal atom
text: Define the central metal atom.

points.text: The metal atom or ion to which a set of ligands is bonded in a fixed geometry.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:the coordination sphere
text: Define the coordination sphere.

points.text: The central metal and its ligands, written within square brackets.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a monodentate ligand

subject: chemistry

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a polydentate ligand

points.text: A ligand that binds through several donor atoms.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:an ambidentate ligand
text: Define an ambidentate ligand.

points.text: A ligand that can bind through either of two different atoms, such as NO₂⁻ or SCN⁻.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:the oxidation number of the central metal

points.text: The charge it would carry if all its ligands were removed with their electron pairs.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a homoleptic complex
text: Define a homoleptic complex.

points.text: A complex in which all the ligands are the same.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a heteroleptic complex
text: Define a heteroleptic complex.

points.text: A complex with more than one kind of ligand.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:ionisation isomerism
text: Define ionisation isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism in which a ligand and a counter ion change places, so that the complexes give different ions in solution.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:linkage isomerism
text: Define linkage isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism in which an ambidentate ligand binds through a different donor atom.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:coordination isomerism
text: Define coordination isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism in which ligands are exchanged between the cationic and anionic complexes of a salt.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:hydrate isomerism
text: Define hydrate isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism in which water changes between being a ligand and being free in the crystal.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:geometrical isomerism
text: Define geometrical isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism due to different relative positions of the ligands around the metal, as in cis and trans forms.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:optical isomerism
text: Define optical isomerism.

points.text: Isomerism in which two forms are non-superimposable mirror images.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:crystal field stabilisation energy
text: Define crystal field stabilisation energy.

points.text: The lowering in energy of a metal’s d electrons by the splitting of their orbitals in a ligand field.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a low spin complex
text: Define a low spin complex.

points.text: A complex in which the d electrons pair up, as the splitting is large, leaving few unpaired.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:a high spin complex
text: Define a high spin complex.

points.text: A complex in which the d electrons stay unpaired as far as possible, as the splitting is small.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:Werner’s primary valency
text: Define Werner’s primary valency.

points.text: The ionisable valency of a central metal, equal to its oxidation state and satisfied by negative ions.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:Werner’s secondary valency
text: Define Werner’s secondary valency.

points.text: The non-ionisable valency of a central metal, equal to its coordination number and fixed in space.

facts: c12-5a:[Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is diamagnetic, while [NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic.
text: Give a reason: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is diamagnetic, while [NiCl₄]²⁻ is paramagnetic.

points.text: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, which pairs the d electrons, giving dsp².
Cl⁻ is weak, so the electrons stay unpaired, giving sp³.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:Tetrahedral complexes are usually high spin.
text: Give a reason: Tetrahedral complexes are usually high spin.

points.text: Their splitting is small, about four ninths of the octahedral value.
So electrons don’t pair up.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:Chelate complexes are especially stable.
text: Give a reason: Chelate complexes are especially stable.

points.text: A ligand with two donor atoms forms a ring with the metal.
That makes the ligand harder to remove, and gives a favourable entropy change.

points.text: Ti³⁺ has one d electron, which can undergo a d–d transition.
Sc³⁺ has no d electrons, so no transition is possible.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is an inner orbital complex and is diamagnetic.
text: Give a reason: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is an inner orbital complex and is diamagnetic.

points.text: NH₃ here acts as a strong-field ligand, which pairs the d electrons.
So d²sp³ hybridisation is used, with no unpaired electrons.

subject: chemistry
facts: c12-5a:[CoF₆]³⁻ is an outer orbital complex and is paramagnetic.
text: Give a reason: [CoF₆]³⁻ is an outer orbital complex and is paramagnetic.

points.text: F⁻ is a weak-field ligand, and doesn’t pair the d electrons.
So sp³d² hybridisation is used, with four unpaired electrons.
